candidates.summary: max(nextNum[key], span.Num) moves every else-if's own IfStmt from Num 0 to Num 2, so the Go2Gno Num=1 wrapper mark (go2gno.go:599) never leaves the nested IfStmt on the span it 'already owns' and adds nothing to uniqueness
candidates.failure_scenario: `if a {} else if b {}`: the wrapper IfCaseStmt enters first with Num 1, so nextNum becomes 2; the nested IfStmt (Num 0) gets max(2,0)=2 and its empty else (Num 1 from setNodeLines) gets 3. The counter alone already yields distinct Nums per (Pos,End) whatever Go2Gno sets, so the go2gno hunk is redundant, and no node keeps Location S#0, which at base resolved to the nested IfStmt. Measured over examples/, gnovm/stdlibs and gnovm/tests/files: 254 IfStmt 0->2, 254 wrappers 0->1, 136 empty elses 1->3, in 52 example files. No FuncDecl/FuncLitExpr/FileNode moves, so today's TypeIDs and persisted FuncValue sources are unaffected; the cost is two mechanisms for one invariant, one of them inert, and a gratuitous Location shift for every deployed else-if IfStmt that any future Location keying (#6060) inherits. Fix: drop the go2gno hunk, or bump Num only when the node's own (Pos,End,Num) is already taken so the IfStmt keeps Num 0.
